mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: court registry issuance, then Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs affixes an Apostille, then submission to the receiving registry in an Apostille Convention state. Consular path: court registry issuance, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization certification, then legalization by the receiving state's embassy or consulate in Korea, then submission to the receiving registry in a non-Apostille state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) through the competent district court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: court registry issuance, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille, then submission in an Apostille Convention state. Consular path: court registry issuance, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular certification, then foreign embassy/consulate legalization in Korea, then submission in a non-Apostille state. The two paths are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation Filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for receiving authorities in Apostille Convention states; alternatively, notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular certification, and consular legalization by the receiving state's embassy in Korea for non-Apostille states. Only one path applies; sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa and its founding shareholders, registered with the Seoul Central District Court and certified by the court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified court copy, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention member states; alternatively, certified court copy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular certification, and embassy/consulate legalization for non-member states. Apostille and consular legalization are alternatives, not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Commercial Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed commercial bank operating in South Korea with an established USD Swift and Fedwire payment rail profile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank issuance, notarization by a Korean notary, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for receiving banks or regulators in Apostille Convention states; for non-Apostille states, bank issuance, notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular certification, and legalization by the receiving state's consulate in Korea. Use exactly one authentication path and never the other sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding or filing, every UBO, director, officer, attorney-in-fact, charter counterparty, aircraft operator, and beneficiary bank must be screened in real time against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and the OFAC 50 Percent Rule, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea Financial Intelligence Unit domestic sanctions designations. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all foreign politically exposed persons and their close associates, plus Korean domestic PEPs holding sensitive public roles. Screening must verify 25 percent ownership layers, adverse media, bankruptcy, tax evasion indicators, and risk-based phonetic name matching. A documented false-positive resolution process and contemporaneous risk rating must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) Company Name Search and Corporation Registration portal (www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be filed in the Korean alphabet Hangul as the controlling legal name. A parallel English trade name may be registered for cross-border charter contracts but must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the Hangul name. Four-tier hierarchy is required: (1) entity suffix such as Yuhan Hoesa, (2) main trade name, (3) operational descriptor such as Air Cargo Charter Broker, and (4) foreign or branch identifier. The exact Hangul spelling controls for registry, tax, customs, and banking purposes; any English transliteration must be marked as an alias.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant shall file a written objection with the registration department of the competent district court within fourteen days of the rejection notice. The objection must state the exact desired name, cite the Korean Commercial Act and court registration rules, demonstrate non-identical trademark and company service, and attach a renewed name search result. If the objection is denied, the applicant may petition for a court ruling in non-contentious litigation, while simultaneously filing a fresh name reservation to avoid pipeline delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected for this licensed air cargo charter broker. The National Tax Service, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and Korean banks expect a dedicated physical office. For an entity holding an air cargo charter brokerage license, business supervision and anti-tax avoidance rules require identifiable premises, regular attendance, books and records at the office, and authority to manage charter contracts in Korea. A shared mail forwarding address is not acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease contract under the company name; (2) utility and internet bills; (3) exterior signage; (4) board minutes at the registered office; (5) payroll and employment records; (6) original charter broker contracts; (7) VAT and tax invoice register. Quantified risk: high; approximately 40 percent likelihood of an unannounced inspection by the local National Tax Service or Seoul city tax authority within the first two years of operation, particularly before VAT registration finalization and upon any license application.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 288-289 (incorporation), 290-292 (articles of incorporation), 293-295 (subscription of shares), 296-300 (incorporation procedures), 302-303 (registration), 306-307 (directors), 312-313 (statutory officers), 317 (registration of incorporation); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (외국인투자촉진법) Articles 2, 5-6 for non-resident ownership; Framework Act on the Administration of Registration (상업등기법) for registry filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registry Office (서울중앙지방법원 등기국) or the local district court registry with jurisdiction over the registered office address; for foreign investment, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest Korea One-Stop Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Application (법인설립등기신청서) filed with the court registry, accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation (정관), subscription agreement, and capital contribution verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korea does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). However, the Articles of Incorporation must specify the total authorized capital and the initial paid-in amount. For foreign investors, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires a minimum foreign investment of KRW 100 million (approximately USD 75,000) to qualify for foreign investment incentives and automatic approval under the Foreign Investment Notification system. The capital must be deposited into a temporary bank account in the name of the entity during incorporation and released upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 368(4) OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF SOUTH KOREA

WHEREAS, the undersigned, being all of the directors of [Company Name] (the 'Company'), a Yuhan Hoesa duly organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, do hereby consent to and adopt the following resolutions as of the date set forth below, with full knowledge that such resolutions shall have the same force and effect as if adopted at a duly convened meeting of the Board of Directors.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire authorized share capital of the Company, consisting of [NUMBER] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [AMOUNT] each, for a total consideration of KRW [TOTAL]. The Board acknowledges that the full subscription amount has been paid in cash into the Company's designated bank account, and the corresponding share certificates shall be issued to the subscribers in accordance with Article 302 of the Commercial Act.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: The Board hereby adopts the registered office of the Company at [FULL ADDRESS], Republic of Korea, as the principal place of business and statutory seat for all legal and administrative purposes. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease agreements and to file all necessary notices with the competent registry authority.

3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: The Board hereby appoints the following individuals to the offices indicated, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are duly elected and qualified: (a) [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director, with full authority to represent the Company in all dealings with third parties, banks, and government authorities; (b) [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, with authority to manage the Company's financial affairs, sign tax filings, and maintain accounting records; (c) [NAME] as Company Secretary, responsible for maintaining corporate records and ensuring compliance with statutory obligations. Each officer shall have the powers and duties as prescribed by the Commercial Act and the Company's Articles of Incorporation.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of bank accounts with [BANK NAME] and [BANK NAME] and designates the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer as the sole signatories for all transactions, with a dual-signature requirement for any transaction exceeding KRW [THRESHOLD]. The Board further authorizes the execution of all necessary banking resolutions, mandates, and wire transfer instructions, including SWIFT and Fedwire payment rails, in accordance with the Company's treasury policy.

5. REGISTRATION AND FILING: The Board directs the Company Secretary to file all required incorporation documents with the competent registry authority, including the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, and the list of directors and officers, within the statutory period of 14 days from the date of this resolution. The Board further authorizes the engagement of a licensed attorney or certified public accountant to facilitate the registration process.

6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes any director or officer to execute, deliver, and file any and all documents, agreements, and instruments necessary to carry out the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to tax registrations, business licenses, and industrial permits.

This resolution is effective immediately upon execution and shall be recorded in the minutes of the Board of Directors.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution as of the date first written above.

[Signature of Director 1] [Signature of Director 2] [Signature of Director 3]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Online Registration System (IRO) at www.iros.go.kr; local bank branch for capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the proposed company name (Korean name) via the I-RO system to ensure no conflict with existing registered entities. The name must include 'Yuhan Hoesa' or 'LLC' as a suffix. Simultaneously, open a temporary capital deposit account at a Korean bank in the name of the future entity, and deposit the initial paid-in capital (if any). Obtain a certificate of deposit balance from the bank, which will be required for registration. For foreign investors, file a Foreign Investment Notification with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank to secure legal status and tax benefits. Ensure all documents are notarized if executed abroad, and apostilled or consularized as per the Hague Convention.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of directors and shareholders
Power of attorney if using a local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and re-file. If the capital deposit is insufficient, increase the deposit and obtain a new certificate. For foreign investment notification issues, consult KOTRA to rectify the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) in Korea; legal counsel for drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in Korean, including mandatory clauses: company name, purpose (air cargo charter brokerage), total authorized shares, par value, registered office address, names of initial directors and auditors, and method of public notice. The Articles must be signed by all incorporators and notarized by a Korean notary public. If any incorporator is outside Korea, execute a power of attorney in favor of a local representative and notarize/apostille the signature. The notarized Articles are a prerequisite for registration. Ensure the business purpose explicitly covers ISIC 5229 activities, including international air freight forwarding, charter brokerage, and ancillary logistics services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, amend the Articles and re-notarize. If the business purpose is too narrow, expand the scope to include related activities to avoid future amendments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (법원등기국) with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the court registry within 14 days of notarization. Submit the notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, and the application form (법인설립등기신청서). The application must include the company name, registered office, total capital, directors' and auditors' details, and the representative director's signature. Pay the registration fee (approximately KRW 180,000, ~USD 150). The court will review the documents and issue the Certificate of Incorporation (법인등기부등본). This certificate is the legal proof of the company's existence. For foreign investors, also submit the Foreign Investment Notification certificate to the registry to ensure proper recording.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query or suspension, respond within the given deadline (usually 2 weeks) by providing additional documents or corrections. If the application is rejected, rectify the issues and re-file. Seek legal assistance if the rejection is based on substantive defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Business License Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system; local district tax office; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) for air freight forwarding license
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, register for corporate tax and business operations with the NTS. Obtain a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) by filing the application online or at the local tax office. This certificate is required for all commercial activities, including opening bank accounts and issuing invoices. Additionally, for air cargo charter brokerage, apply for a Freight Forwarding License (국제물류주선업 등록) from MOLIT under the Aviation Business Act. The application must include the business registration certificate, proof of office space, and a business plan. The license is mandatory for operating as an air cargo charter broker. Also, register for value-added tax (VAT) and corporate tax with the NTS. For foreign-owned entities, ensure compliance with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting.
required_dossiers: Business plan for air freight forwarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS delays the business registration, follow up with the local tax office. If MOLIT rejects the license application, review the business plan and financial capacity, and re-apply. For tax issues, consult a certified tax accountant (CTA) to resolve discrepancies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) – Aviation Policy Division; also the Korea Customs Service for bonded cargo operations if applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Freight Forwarding Business Registration (국제운송주선업 등록) under the Aviation Business Act (항공사업법) Article 2(3) and Enforcement Decree Article 3

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (ME) – Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – The business is a pure brokerage and administrative service for air cargo charter, with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing operations. No EIA is required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (환경영향평가법) Schedule 1-3, as the activity does not involve construction, land development, or industrial facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation. However, the office premises must comply with general waste disposal regulations under the Waste Management Act (폐기물관리법), and any electronic equipment disposal must follow the Act on Resource Circulation of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (전기·전자제품 및 자동차의 자원순환에 관한 법률).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (소방안전증명) from the National Fire Agency (소방청) for the registered office, confirming compliance with the Fire Prevention and Safety Act (소방시설법) – including installation of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and fire alarm systems. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act (산업안전보건법) for the office workplace, including a general safety inspection and employee health check program. For any temporary storage of cargo documents or samples, a separate warehouse permit is not required as the business does not hold physical inventory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax electronic tax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS portal (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register with the competent district tax office through HomeTax or in person before commencing any Korean VAT-taxable air cargo charter brokerage activity. For a Yuhan Hoesa, file the standard business registration application with the articles of incorporation, domestic place of business documentation, shareholding and ultimate beneficial ownership information, designated bank account details, and proof of the business premise. A foreign non-resident entity with a Korean tax presence must obtain a Business Operator Registration Number, which serves as the Korean Tax Identification Number (TIN/VAT ID), by applying for either a domestic business registration or a Foreign Business Operator registration through HomeTax and, where required, appointing a tax representative in Korea for VAT payment and refund administration. Separately, for customs obligations, the entity must obtain a Customs Business Code from the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS. When acting solely as an air cargo charter broker or international freight forwarder, the entity must document that it is not the exporter of record unless it holds export authority; the brokerage income will be classified as a Korean export service connected to goods that cross the Korean border.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Korean Commercial Act, a separate legal person subject to Korean corporate income tax on worldwide income, with no transparent or pass-through classification for Korean tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Korea has no check-the-box election for entity classification and no hybrid mismatch entity election. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a corporation. VAT simplified taxpayer treatment may apply when annual taxable turnover is KRW 80 million or less, but that is an indirect tax compliance simplification, not an income tax classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary exemption threshold for VAT registration; any business operator with a Korean taxable supply nexus must register from the commencement of business. A reduced-compliance simplified taxable person status applies where annual taxable turnover is KRW 80 million or less, but this threshold is not a registration exemption and does not apply to a foreign entity transactionally placed as a general taxable person.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for supplies made to other business operators through the NTS e-tax invoice system on HomeTax. Tax invoices must be issued electronically by the day following the taxable supply date through HomeTax or an approved API-connected ERP system; the NTS receives the electronic tax invoice data in near real time. Korea does not operate a per-transaction fiscal stamp clearance model, but the NTS applies data matching and compliance analytics across HomeTax, foreign exchange settlement records, and the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system to detect missing or manipulated invoices, omitted supply, and anti-fraud anomalies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where goods are exported under an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, and for qualifying services supplied to non-residents, including international air cargo transportation, freight forwarding, and cargo charter brokerage, when the place of supply is outside Korea or the service directly supports cargo exported from Korea. The entity must establish through the charter agreement, commercial invoice, air waybill, and foreign exchange settlement that the underlying cargo is transported internationally, and that the service is supplied to a foreign principal or a Korean business in connection with an export transaction. Services performed wholly or partly in the domestic Korean market, including domestic cabotage air movement, import-related warehousing, or brokerage of domestic transportation, are outside the export zero-rating provision and are taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: KCS export declaration acceptance record (electronic Export Declaration in UNI-PASS)
Air Waybill (MAWB/HAWB) evidencing international carriage of the cargo from Korea to the overseas destination
Commercial invoice and charter-party or forwarding contract between the Korean broker and the foreign principal
Packing list, cargo manifest, and, where applicable, certificate of origin
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of the foreign currency export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is retrospective and may be clawed back where the supporting documentation is absent, unreliable, mismatched, or created solely to obtain an export VAT refund. If zero-rating is denied, the NTS assesses output VAT at the standard 10% rate on the relevant supply, adds statutory late-payment interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and imposes penalty taxes as prescribed by the Value-Added Tax Act, including penalties for false or unfaithful tax invoices. Failure to collect export proceeds within the 180-day foreign exchange repatriation deadline, or without an approved extension, can cause denial of zero-rating and liability under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including fines or imprisonment. Fraudulent export VAT refunds are additionally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the statutory audit lookback periods allow the tax authority to reach back up to 10 years for fraudulent tax evasion cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (South Korea) alongside the Ministry of Economy and Finance, jointly administering the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a predominantly liberalised yet closely monitored foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is free for current account transactions such as trade in goods and services, freight and charter hire payments, and ordinary business expenses, which are settled through licensed foreign exchange banks without prior approval. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity investment, cross-border loans, and outbound direct investment, remain subject to mandatory reporting, declaration, or prior approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For an air cargo charter broker in the form of a Yuhan Hoesa, the key friction points are the generation, retention, and repatriation of export service proceeds, as well as the statutory requirement to receive export-related foreign currency within a defined period. While there is no blanket surrender-and-convert obligation compelling firms to exchange all foreign currency into Korean won, companies are required to collect export proceeds into a domestic foreign exchange bank account or, subject to reporting, may hold them offshore. Profit remittances by foreign shareholders are permitted once corporate tax obligations and capital verification are satisfied, but the bank must receive a standard tax clearance certificate and a foreign exchange report confirming the remittance purpose. In practice, convertibility is robust for genuine trade and investment flows, but any deviation from the declared business purpose, round-tripping structures, or undocumented use of overseas accounts will trigger immediate rejection or enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korean exporters and service providers must collect and repatriate export-related foreign currency receipts within six months from the date of the export declaration or, for cross-border services, completion of the service. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won; proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in a domestic foreign exchange bank account, but any non-reporting of offshore retention or delayed repatriation beyond the statutory timeline without prior approval constitutes a violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Proceeds Receipt Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. As a direct matter of Korean law, fintech electronic money institutions and offshore digital EMIs do not possess the statutory authority to open bank accounts that can receive export proceeds, effect capital verification, or engage in foreign exchange clearing on behalf of a domestic Korean legal entity. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act confines licensed foreign exchange business to registered banks and authorised brokerages. Offshore EMIs operating purely on a payment-institution licence in another jurisdiction cannot clear Korean won or access the local settlement infrastructure. Accordingly, the treasury blueprint must rely exclusively on Tier-1 domestic commercial banks for all regulatory capital and trade settlement flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa must normally present at least one authorised signatory or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact for physical or supervised remote identification. Most Korean Tier-1 banks require the statutory director or a Power of Attorney holder to attend a face-to-face interview at a domestic branch for initial onboarding. Remote video-based KYC is accepted only in limited cases where the ultimate beneficial owner is a highly rated financial institution or holds an accredited verification certificate. A consular notarisation of the Power of Attorney at a Korean embassy may allow a local representative to open the account without the statutory director being physically present, but the bank's compliance committee still requires the beneficial owner and signatories to undergo liveliness and sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain for the non-resident Korean LLC, particularly if ultimate ownership is spread through offshore directorships or nominee shareholding arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full corporate diagram showing the ultimate beneficial owner and all intermediate entities, certified copies of certificates of incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, notarised power of attorney, and a sworn equity declaration. For each non-resident owner, provide passport copies, a source of wealth statement supported by audited financial statements, and a bank reference letter from the originating jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering exposure tied to air cargo charter brokering, where third-party payees or freight forwarders differ from the named airline and charter operator on the underlying contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed charter service agreements, detailed commercial invoices, invoicing reasonableness analyses, original or certified airway bills, bank remittance instructions, a breakdown of commission versus pass-through costs, and slot or route contracts. The compliance committee will also expect a written explanation for any deviation between the counterparty on the contract and the beneficiary on the settlement transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient source of funds for the initial capital injection or high-volume inbound remittances intended to prepay aircraft charter capacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive source of funds evidence comprising the corporate parent's audited financial statements, shareholder deposit receipts, loan agreements if funding is debt-based, personal tax returns and bank statements for shareholders, and the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Confirmation. All remittances must be tied to the foreign investment declaration and show a clear purpose code matching the air cargo charter business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed person intersection for cargo routes and charter payment clearing, where the broker may touch sanctioned jurisdictions or restricted airlines
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A continuous sanctions screening report covering all directors, beneficial owners, and counterparties against UN, OFAC, EU, and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit lists, certificates of no adverse media, air operator certificates of the chartered carriers, and a route legality opinion confirming that no chartered aircraft will overfly or land in any embargoed country.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Yuhan Hoesa must be routed through the designated Tier-1 domestic bank under an official foreign investment declaration submitted to the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The remitting shareholder should use a SWIFT MT103 wire with a correct foreign exchange purpose code, typically the code for direct equity investment or paid-in capital. The receiving domestic bank verifies the declaration, issues a Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Confirmation, and records the capital in the company's capital verification ledger. All KRW conversion, if required, is executed at the applicable market rate through the licensed bank. Cash injections through unauthorised channels or fintech wallets are prohibited and will be deemed non-compliant.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for air cargo charter settlements are SWIFT MT103 for direct cash payments to airlines, handling agents, and fuel suppliers; commercial letters of credit through MT700 or MT710 when the beneficiary bank requires documentary assurance; and documentary collections where the air carrier presents title documents and charter invoices. KRW-denominated obligations may clear through the local Korean Won Settlement System, but all cross-border portions must be processed via authenticated SWIFT messages. Export service receipts should be first credited to the foreign currency account and then disbursed only after matching the underlying charter contract and invoice references.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with a Korean Tier-1 bank limited to real trade and charter settlement exposures
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts available for Korean won hedging where the underlying charter invoice is settled in US dollars but the operating margin is KRW-denominated
Currency swaps executed with licensed Korean banks for aligning large aircraft lease payments in USD with operating revenue in KRW, requiring documented underlying cash flow exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Management Report (if any foreign investor holds equity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Foreign Investment Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar fiscal year ending 31 December, the report is due no later than 15 February of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, due within 45 days after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 2,000,000 (approximately USD 1,500) for failure to file or for material false filing; repeated noncompliance may cause the foreign investment to lose statutory recognition, incentive eligibility, and Foreign Investment Promotion Act protections, but does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year, the deadline is 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid corporate tax accrues late-payment surcharge at approximately 0.022% per day from the statutory due date; failure to file within the deadline attracts an additional 20% penalty on the unpaid tax, or up to 0.5% per month for unfiled tax capped at 36 months; after demand and continued nonpayment, the NTS may seize corporate assets, cancel the business registration after two consecutive years of non-filing, and the registry court may dissolve the entity upon application by the tax authority or an interested party.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Income Tax Surtax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered business district (si, gun, or gu) via the SeTax local tax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The local income surtax on corporate income is paid together with the national corporate income tax return, generally by 31 March for calendar-year entities; in jurisdictions that issue separate billing, payment is required by the end of the month following the national filing date (normally 30 April).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Overdue local income surtax accrues local tax delinquency additional charges (approximately 0.022% per day or statutory local surcharge equivalent) plus late-filing penalties of up to 20%; prolonged default permits a local tax lien, asset seizure, and an application to the court for dissolution if the business registration remains delinquent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for audit report filing by the certified public accountant; audited financial statements accompany the National Tax Service annual corporate tax return where required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent audit must be completed before the annual general meeting of members; for a 31 December fiscal year the audited statements should be ready for attachment to the 31 March corporate tax return, and the audit report must be filed with the FSS within two weeks after the annual general meeting, in all cases by no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or file an external audit report when statutorily required constitutes a violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, subject to corrective orders, publication of sanctions, and administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000; unapproved audited statements cannot support dividend distributions or valid tax filings, and persistent noncompliance may result in NTS referral and court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Members (internal statutory corporate organ; not a government authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year, no later than 30 June of the following year, with notice provided to members at least two weeks before the meeting under the Commercial Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A member may petition the court to compel convening of the meeting; failure to approve the annual accounts prevents lawful dividend distributions and completion of statutory filings; directors may face fines up to KRW 5,000,000 for obstruction of inspection or failure to make financial statements available, and continued malfunction of corporate organs may become grounds for court-ordered dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is subject to a mandatory independent audit by a certified public accountant if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, any of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million); (ii) annual revenue from air cargo brokerage, charter fees, and related service income equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 75 million); or (iii) the average number of regular employees equals or exceeds 300. A statutory audit is also compulsory if the company has made a public offering of securities, has publicly issued debt instruments, or is designated by the Financial Supervisory Service as a public-interest company; the FSS may also require audit designation for a company facing material solvency or transparency risk.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to public-interest entities and to companies that voluntarily adopt K-IFRS; non-listed private Yuhan Hoesa entities that are not public-interest companies may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), specifically the accounting standards for corporations under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, while micro-entities may keep statutory tax-basis books that are reconciled to GAAP when an audit becomes mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose a standalone annual UBO return for an ordinary private Yuhan Hoesa, but beneficial ownership is confirmed through the register of members and the annual foreign investment management report. Any transfer of a foreign-invested equity interest must be reported through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act protocol within 30 days of the closing date; under the Commercial Act, an equity transfer becomes effective as against the company only after it is entered in the register of members, and any change of directors or statutory representative must be filed with the registry court within 14 days. The company must maintain a current beneficial-ownership schedule for National Tax Service transparency review and must respond to any NTS notice requiring real-beneficiary disclosure within the stated response period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages (including pledged quota interests)
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,000 per year for a commercial registered office and licensed corporate secretarial agent in metropolitan Seoul; provincial registered offices generally range from USD 300 to USD 700.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 per year depending on asset size, transaction volume, and complexity of the air cargo charter brokerage; a medium-risk entity with international wire transactions typically falls in the USD 8,000 - USD 18,000 range.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.4% (24% national top corporate tax rate plus 10% local income tax surcharge)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises may enjoy up to a 5-year corporate income tax holiday under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and technology-intensive operations may receive an additional R&D expense credit of up to 20% under the R&D tax incentive regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korea Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 110) and related schedules; filed electronically through the HomeTax system (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return and audited financial statements must be filed by March 31 of the following fiscal year; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The unique 10-digit tax identification number assigned by the Korean National Tax Service.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the active BRN of the Korean entity; even if the Korean entity is 100% foreign-owned, the BRN must be live and correspond to the entity's head office address in Korea. The foreign parent must appoint a local tax manager or statutory representative for all correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of the foreign shareholders' names, countries of residence, shareholding percentages, and tax identification numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the legal entity name and country of residence of each ultimate non-resident shareholder. Attach a Tax Residency Certificate to substantiate treaty eligibility for dividend withholding relief. In absence of a valid certificate, the statutory 22% withholding will apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Any transfer pricing adjustment made to the taxable income due to international intercompany transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directly enter the net upward adjustment attributable to non-compliance with the arm's-length principle. The schedule must reference the intercompany agreements for the charter brokerage, including charter hire payments, administrative service charges, and commission splits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income taxes paid to non-Korean jurisdictions on foreign-source income included in the Korean taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the foreign tax credit limitation computed on the basis of Korean tax rate. For a non-resident charter broker, revenue earned from foreign carriers and cargo owners may be foreign-source only if the contract is concluded through a foreign permanent establishment; otherwise, the income is taxed in Korea with a tax credit for any foreign tax withheld.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of treaty benefits claimed against Korean taxation of foreign-source income or distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident shareholder claims a reduced withholding rate or a tax credit under a DTA, this schedule must identify the treaty article and include the Foreign Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership statement. If no benefits are claimed, write 'NIL' explicitly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 66 - Payments to Non-Resident Home Office or Affiliates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts paid to overseas head offices, branches, or affiliates for royalties, interests, charters, and service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fully itemise any remittance for aircraft charter, brokerage fees, or marketing support provided by a non-resident affiliate. The Korean tax assessor will apply a 22% withholding tax on deemed royalty or service fees, and deductibility may be denied if the payment does not meet the arm's-length standard and economic benefit test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return triggers an additional penalty of 20% of the amount of unpaid tax. The amount of unpaid tax additionally bears a daily surcharge of 0.022% per day (equivalent to 8.03% annually) until fully paid. In case of deliberate omission, a 10% penalty on the unnecessarily low amount is imposed, and a criminal referral under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act may lead to imprisonment of up to 7 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, resulting in 22% effective withholding on outbound dividends to non-residents).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Bilateral DTA relief must be claimed in the following order: (1) obtain the Tax Residency Certificate from the foreign tax authority, (2) fill in the 'Application for Conditional Tax Exemption/Levy Reduction' (HomeTax form schedule 42-23), (3) attach a beneficial ownership declaration and a shareholder certificate evidencing ownership of the Korean entity, and (4) submit these to the local District Tax Office or the paying agent before the dividend declaration date. The tax office may then grant a reduced rate in real time; any excess withheld tax can be claimed as a refund under Article 88 of the Corporate Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rates are 20% withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents, plus surcharge, giving 22% effective WHT. Under the Korea-United States DTA, royalty and interest rates are reduced to 10%; under the Korea-Japan DTA, the rate may be reduced to 10% for royalties and 5% for interest under certain conditions (for Japanese financial institutions). The benefit is conditional upon the payee being the beneficial owner and on compliance with substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File must be prepared when the amount of intra-group cross-border transactions with foreign related entities exceeds KRW 5 billion (about USD 3.8 million) during a fiscal year. For transactions in the range of KRW 1 billion to KRW 5 billion, simplified documentation is still required if the taxpayer's total revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Korean tax authorities apply the substance-over-form principle and the international tax abuse rule to deny treaty benefits when an entity does not have the required economic substance. For an air cargo charter broker, the Korean entity must have adequate personnel, an office, and a real decision-making capability in treasury, charter negotiation, and invoicing; if not, the Korean entity may be disregarded as a "sham", and profits are reattributed to its beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly underreporting charter brokerage fees or fabricating documents to reduce Korean corporate income tax, e.g., booking charter income to a foreign shell entity without actual agency relationship.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4(1) of the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act imposes up to 7 years imprisonment and a fine equal to not less than 2 times but not exceeding 3 times the amount of corporate tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where a director has made a false statement in the tax return. The director is personally liable for the fine, and the director's assets are subject to attachment. A travel ban (departure prohibition) will be issued by the National Tax Service while the case is under investigation. The director may also be personally disqualified for 5 years from holding any corporate office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and submit the Local File/Master File on time or knowingly submitting false intercompany arm's-length analysis (e.g., omitting a 40% related-party charter margin).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 12(2) of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) allows an up to 30% penalty on the under-recalculated taxable income in addition to re-assessed tax, and a 10% surcharge on the difference.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's transfer pricing penalty only if the failure was due to gross negligence or willful intent. In addition, the courts may order the director to reimburse the company for the amount of fines under the Korean Commercial Act, and a criminal charge of tax fraud may be filed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Korean LLC in name only, i.e., no office, no personnel, no negotiation authority, and relying entirely on the overseas parent for all charter negotiations and invoicing, yet claiming treaty benefits for dividends while not paying adequate Korean tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 49(2) of the Framework Act on International Tax Affairs empowers the tax authority to ignore the entity and reassess income to the beneficial owner, applying a penalty of 40% of the unreported offshore income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: This triggers lifting the veil: the director becomes personally liable for the reassessed corporate taxes and penalties to the extent the corporate assets are insufficient. Remedies also include a court order prohibiting the director from leaving the country, and under the Tax Fraud Punishment Act, potential imprisonment for organising the sham structure.
